title: What causes rigor mortis?
summary: Josh and Chuck explain rigor mortis: the story of Val Thomas, a West Virginia woman who reportedly came back after rigor mortis set in; the Shroud of Turin cadaver experiments and crucifixion through the wrist; the physiology of muscle contraction (calcium ions, myosin and actin, ATP) and why it stops with decay (autolysis); factors that speed or slow onset and duration (temperature, fat, age, exertion, cold); cadaveric spasm; and other postmortem clues used by forensic investigators (livor mortis, algor mortis, stomach contents, blow fly maggot development). The episode ends with a listener mail from David in Atlanta about a Ponzi-style real estate scheme he encountered while doing IT work.
topics: stiffening of the body after death
blue bottle fly maggots forensic entomology

segments.title: Opening banter and Val Thomas story
segments.summary: Hosts banter about the show opening, then tell the story of Val Thomas, who reportedly woke up after about seventeen hours dead with rigor mortis already set in.

segments.title: Cadavers, Stiff, and the Shroud of Turin
segments.summary: Discussion of Mary Roach's book Stiff and a late nineteenth-century French physician who used cadavers to test whether Christ could have been crucified through the palms, finding the wrists would hold a body.

segments.title: Onset of rigor mortis: timing and head-to-toe pattern
segments.summary: Rigor mortis begins about three hours after death and proceeds from head to toe, attributed to the delicate facial muscles stiffening first; Euston is named as the discoverer.

segments.title: Muscle physiology and the biochemistry of stiffening
segments.summary: Explanation of skeletal versus smooth muscle, motor neurons, calcium ions, myosin and actin binding, and ATP's role in relaxation; after death, lack of oxygen and ATP and calcium buildup cause contraction.

segments.title: Duration of rigor mortis and factors affecting it
segments.summary: Rigor lasts roughly twelve to eighteen hours, depending on conditions. Warmth speeds onset and shortens duration through decay and autolysis; cold slows it and can prolong it. Cadaveric spasm, fat, and age also affect timing.

segments.title: Other postmortem clues for forensic investigators
segments.summary: Rigor mortis is imprecise for time of death, so investigators use livor mortis (lividity), algor mortis (cooling, about 1.5 to 2 degrees per hour), stomach contents, and blue bottle fly maggot development.

segments.title: Wrap-up and promised future episodes
segments.summary: Hosts agree to do future episodes on body farms and forensic pathology, then move to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail: David in Atlanta on a Ponzi-style scheme
segments.summary: David recounts doing IT work for a Atlanta real estate company that showed red flags such as heavy security and a ban on Georgia investors; it collapsed after about a month, leaving him unpaid.
